title: Full Eigenstate Thermalization in Quantum Field Theory and Gravitational Scrambling
abstract: Using thermal analyticity, we derive directional large-frequency bounds on the smooth functions entering full eigenstate thermalization in continuum quantum field theory. The strongest directions reproduce the scales previously identified for lattice systems, while the complete analyticity domain reveals an asymmetric multifrequency structure. Thermal conformal correlators saturate the second- and third-order bounds, and the leading gravitational Regge contribution saturates the strongest fourth-order direction.
summary: This paper derives rigorous, directional bounds on the correlation functions characterizing full eigenstate thermalization in QFT. By analyzing the analyticity domain in the complex frequency plane, the authors demonstrate that both CFT correlators and gravitational scattering processes saturate these bounds. This provides strong evidence that holographic models realize the full constraints predicted by ETH in continuum quantum systems.
main_problem: To derive directional large-frequency bounds on the smooth functions governing full eigenstate thermalization (full ETH) in continuum quantum field theory (QFT) and holographic systems.
main_result: The analysis shows that thermal conformal correlators saturate the second- and third-order bounds, and the leading gravitational Regge contribution saturates the strongest fourth-order direction, confirming ETH constraints in holographic CFTs.
method: The authors use thermal analyticity, deforming contours in the complex plane, and deriving bounds on free cumulants ($\kappa_n$) to analyze the large-frequency behavior of correlation functions.
model_or_system: The study applies to continuum Quantum Field Theory (QFT) and holographic systems (AdS/CFT), using concepts like Out-of-Time-Order Correlators (OTOCs) and free probability theory to characterize thermalization.
key_observables: Full ETH smooth functions ($F^{(n)}$), thermal free cumulants ($\kappa_n$), two- and three-point correlation functions, and the fourth free cumulant ($\kappa_4$).
important_parameters: Large frequency scale ($W 	o \infty$), energy differences ($\vec{\omega}$), and the inverse temperature ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that the function $C(\vec{\eta})$ is finite in the interior of the analyticity domain and grows at most algebraically near the boundaries.

Figure 2 shows the saturation of the full-ETH bound for the three-point function in 2D CFT.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by using thermal analyticity to derive directional bounds on free cumulants. It then demonstrates the saturation of these bounds using concrete calculations from 2D CFT and holographic models, particularly for the fourth free cumulant.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, continuum field-theoretic method to test the limits of thermalization, which is a central topic in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and quantum chaos, relevant to understanding thermalization in complex quantum systems.
